findings.title: Team-admin permission check uses AND instead of OR, locking out plain team admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamOwner` only returns true for the OWNER role while `isTeamAdmin` returns true for ADMIN or OWNER. Combining them with `&&` means the variable is effectively only true for OWNERs - a plain team ADMIN (who is not also the OWNER) will fail `isTeamOwner` and therefore be denied permission to add guests, even though the variable name and apparent intent ("AdminOrOwner") indicate admins should be allowed. This should be `||`. Consequence: legitimate team admins cannot add guests and will get a FORBIDDEN error.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: The handler fetches `booking.user` with `destinationCalendar` and `credentials` included (lines 35-40), but never uses them. Instead it calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and builds `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` using `ctx.user` - the person making the request (which per the permission logic above can be a team admin or even just an attendee, not necessarily the booking organizer). When the caller is not the organizer, the EventManager will attempt to update the organizer's external calendar event using the caller's own calendar credentials (or lack thereof), which will either silently fail to update the calendar, update the wrong calendar, or throw, since the caller may not have access to the organizer's calendar integration at all.

findings.title: Email classification uses unfiltered guest list instead of the deduplicated list actually added
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw `guests` input, not `uniqueGuests` (the list after filtering out emails that already belong to existing attendees or are blacklisted). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), each existing attendee is sent `AttendeeScheduledEmail` if their email is in this list, or `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` otherwise. If a caller re-submits an email that already belongs to an existing attendee (so it's filtered out and not actually added), that pre-existing attendee is nonetheless treated as "new" and will incorrectly receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` invite instead of (or in addition to) the lighter `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification - a case that can legitimately occur any time the submitted guest list overlaps with current attendees.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive while the blacklist itself is lowercased
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built by lowercasing every entry from `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, but the comparison `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares against the raw, non-lowercased `guest` string. An email that differs only in case from a blacklisted address (e.g. `Spam@Example.com` vs `spam@example.com`) will bypass the blacklist filter entirely, defeating the intended restriction.

findings.title: Server-side schema does not enforce unique guest emails, allowing duplicate attendee rows
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.guests` is just `z.array(z.string().email())`, with no refinement against duplicate entries within the array. The client-side dialog adds its own uniqueness check via a local zod refine, but that is easily bypassed by calling the tRPC mutation directly (or via any other client). The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only removes emails that match *existing* attendees - it does not deduplicate entries within the submitted `guests` array itself - so a payload with the same email repeated multiple times will create multiple attendee rows with an identical email via `createMany`, corrupting booking attendee data.

findings.title: No upper bound on number of guests that can be added per request
findings.body: Any attendee of a booking (not just the organizer/team admin) is permitted to add guests, per the permission check a few lines below, but there is no limit on the size of the `guests` array. A single attendee could submit a very large list of guest emails in one request, causing unbounded attendee record creation, unbounded calendar-attendee updates, and unbounded email sends (invite spam) for a booking they do not own.

findings.title: Email send failures are silently swallowed with console.log and no error detail
findings.body: The `catch (err)` block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`; the actual `err` object is discarded, and this bypasses the project's logger (e.g. `@calcom/lib/logger` used elsewhere in email-manager.ts) used for structured error reporting. This makes it impossible to diagnose production email failures for this feature, and the user is given no indication that guest-notification emails failed even though the booking mutation itself succeeded.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable code
findings.body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (a template literal with at least ": "), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never falls back to the friendlier `unable_to_add_guests` message. If `err.data?.code` or `err.message` is undefined, or `err.message` is not a valid translation key, the user will see a raw/garbled string like `undefined: you_do_not_have_permission` instead of a clean fallback message.

findings.title: Label htmlFor references a non-existent id, breaking label association
findings.body: `<label htmlFor="emails" ...>{label}</label>` targets an element with `id="emails"`, but none of the rendered `EmailField` inputs are given `id="emails"` (or any matching id per field). This breaks the label-to-input association for assistive technology and for click-to-focus behavior, since with multiple emails the label can only ever point at most to one field and in practice points at none.

findings.title: No automated tests for new addGuests permission, email, and calendar-update logic
findings.body: This PR introduces a new tRPC mutation with non-trivial permission logic (organizer/team-admin/attendee checks), a new UI dialog, new email templates, and calendar-attendee update logic, but no unit or integration tests are included anywhere in the diff. Given the permission-check bug and credential-mismatch bug identified in this handler, test coverage (e.g. verifying who can/cannot add guests, that duplicate/blacklisted emails are rejected, and that the correct calendar credentials are used) would have caught these issues before merge.
